text: In Genesis 6 there is a world corrupt all the way down and one man who “walked with God” (Genesis 6:9). The narrator does not soften the corruption: “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” the earth was “filled with violence,” and Yahweh was sorry that he had made man (Genesis 6:5–6, 11). Noah is not charged with reforming that world. He is told to build. More space goes to the ark’s specifications than to the corruption that makes the ark necessary, because Noah builds according to a measure he did not set (Genesis 6:14–16). The ark is first given as dimensions, before it is made from wood. Noah’s part receives only one summary: “Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he” (Genesis 6:22). Genesis 6 names Noah as righteous before he acts, and his righteousness becomes visible as obedience: the willingness to build what the God who has seen the whole world says will be needed.
